smells.finding: build_lap_evidence_records's body (excluding docstring) is ~24 lines: one for-loop, a single-line optional-mapping lookup, one observation_features call, one observation_weight call, one record construction. Shorter than the sibling G2/G3 composers.
No classes defined -- the module is a single free function plus its docstring.

No logic duplicated from fp_representativeness.py (the logistic form is called, never reimplemented -- confirmed no sigmoid/exp/math import in this file) nor from sibling composers (no _none_if_nan-style helper repeated here; this module has no NaN-normalization need since FpLapLatent's fields are already typed non-Optional floats).

The loop reads FpLapLatent's own fields (driver, lap_number, compound, mass_kg, mass_sigma_kg, run_purpose) and passes the whole latent object into observation_features -- exactly this composer's stated job (translate FpLapLatent into LapEvidenceRecord), not reaching into internals to do work that belongs elsewhere.

Two clumps travel together: (year, gp_name, session_type, model_version) as the record's identity, and (quali_fuel_kg, track_evolution, session_max_track_evolution) as observation_features's own feature-computation inputs.

override.repo_standard: src/physics/layer2/fp_lap_latent.py's frozen FpLapLatent dataclass (read-only this gate, per Specific Exclusions) genuinely carries no year/gp_name/session_type fields (confirmed by direct field inspection) -- the identity clump is forced by an already-closed upstream shape, not invented here. The second clump is fp_representativeness.py's own frozen observation_features(latent, *, quali_fuel_kg, track_evolution, session_max_track_evolution) signature (read-only this gate) -- these three names are forwarded verbatim, not re-grouped or renamed locally.
override.reason: Both clumps are pinned by frozen upstream module shapes this gate has no authority to revisit (mirrors G2/G3's own already-logged data-clumps overrides citing G1's frozen record shapes) -- introducing a local value-object here would just re-wrap already-fixed upstream parameter sets for no behavior gain.

smells.finding: track_evolution is a raw dict[int, int]; year/gp_name/session_type/compound/run_purpose are raw int/str throughout, not dedicated value types.

override.repo_standard: src/physics/feature_view/records.py's own docstring: WeekendStateRecord's axis_values/axis_sigma/axis_status "are DICTS keyed by axis name (not fixed columns)"; SESSION_ORDER and session identity fields are plain str/int throughout G1 (frozen). G2/G3 already logged the identical override for the identical string-identity convention.
override.reason: Matches the codebase's own established, repeatedly-reused convention for keyed physics/session data (plain dict, plain str/int identity) across every sibling module in this package -- not an ad hoc primitive shortcut introduced by this diff.

smells.finding: build_lap_evidence_records takes 8 total parameters (1 positional + 7 keyword-only) -- more than any sibling composer in this package (G2: 3, G3: 4). All 8 are individually well-named and keyword-only (no positional-ordering risk), and each is either a record-identity field FpLapLatent genuinely lacks (year/gp_name/session_type/model_version) or a verbatim passthrough of observation_features's own already-fixed optional parameters (quali_fuel_kg/track_evolution/session_max_track_evolution) -- so no parameter was invented gratuitously. Not blocking, but worth naming: if a fifth composer needs the same (year, gp_name, session_type) identity triple, a small shared SessionIdentity-style parameter object across the composer family would be worth considering at that point (non-blocking observation, not a defect in this gate).

Single bounded change (one new module + one new test file); no existing call site required editing (nothing yet imports build_lap_evidence_records -- it is new production code awaiting its real caller, same posture as G2/G3 at their own gates).

The module has exactly one reason to change: how a FpLapLatent becomes a LapEvidenceRecord. Straight-copy fields, the weight computation, and the track_evolution lookup are all facets of that one composition responsibility, not independent axes of change.
No a.b.c.d navigation chains. track_evolution.get(latent.lap_number) is a single dict lookup keyed by a single attribute access; latent.<field> reads are all one level deep.

No unused hooks, abstract base classes, or generality built for a hypothetical future caller. session_max_track_evolution is not a speculative addition -- it is a real, already-existing optional parameter on the upstream observation_features/track_evolution_score functions, forwarded because a real caller (a future within-session normalizer) is named in those functions' own docstrings, not invented here.
The module docstring (~63 lines) and the function's own docstring together substantially exceed the ~24-line function body they describe.
